title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the briefing reports policy activation automation as undocumented, although Microsoft documents a command for changing auto-labeling policy mode. It also treats lower-priority label replacement settings as an unanswered question despite documentation covering policies that apply sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The new auto-labeling policy applies SharePoint document library default sensitivity labels to eligible existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.claim: Previously, default library sensitivity labels applied only to new or modified files, leaving historical files potentially unlabelled.
claims.quote: Previously, default library sensitivity labels were applied only to new or modified files.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users do not need to open or edit existing files for the policy to label them.
claims.quote: Users are not required to open or edit files for labeling to occur.

claims.claim: Sensitive information type and trainable classifier conditions are not required.
claims.quote: Content inspection conditions, such as sensitive information types or trainable classifiers, are not required for this policy.

claims.claim: The policy does not inspect content to choose a label; it uses the library default label setting.
claims.quote: This policy type doesn't inspect file content to choose a label. The label comes from the SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Labelling is a background service process and is not immediate.
claims.quote: Labeling occurs as a background service process and is not immediate.

claims.claim: Files without a sensitivity label receive the library default label.
claims.quote: Files that do not have a sensitivity label applied will receive the library's default sensitivity label.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Files with a lower-priority label may be upgraded depending on the policy setting.
claims.quote: Files that have a lower-priority sensitivity label applied may be upgraded to the library's default sensitivity label (depending on the policy setting).

claims.claim: No documented creation command selects the library-default-label policy subtype.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint document libraries" "auto-labeling" "PowerShell"; read New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy syntax and searched library/default parameters, plus the auto-labeling PowerShell section. Found generic fixed-label creation, not subtype selection.

claims.claim: An administrator can select the policy and Turn on policy from the Purview auto-labeling policies experience.
claims.quote: Select your policy to see the details of the configuration and status ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or API for running or enabling an existing policy of this type.
claims.quote: Use the Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy cmdlet to modify auto-labeling policies in your organization. ... The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level of the auto-labeling policy. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind powershell, call 'Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -Mode Enable', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/set-autosensitivitylabelpolicy'. Add to its note 'Run in Security & Compliance PowerShell.' Replace the blanket prose absence with 'The creation command for selecting this policy subtype is not yet documented; Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy documents changing an existing auto-labeling policy to Mode Enable.' Narrow the automation open question to creation of this subtype.

claims.claim: There is no separately documented feature switch beyond administrator creation and activation of the policy.

claims.claim: Which settings govern replacement of lower-priority labels, including manually applied labels, remains undocumented for this apply-label policy.
claims.quote: For auto-labeling policies that apply a sensitivity label, you can select a setting to override a manually applied label that has lower priority. ... The configurable setting for auto-labeling policies is on the Additional label settings page.
claims.fix: Replace the first Open questions bullet with: 'Learn documents that automatic labeling replaces a lower-priority automatically applied label. For auto-labeling policies that apply a sensitivity label, replacement of a lower-priority manually applied label is configurable on the Additional label settings page; it is off by default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/apply-sensitivity-label-automatically#will-an-existing-label-be-overridden.
